title: Crystal field theory
examples: How does the geometry of the complex affect the splitting pattern?
Can you explain the difference between high and low spin states using an example?
What determines whether a complex will be high spin or low spin?

explain.say: Today we are learning about crystal field theory in chemistry.
When ligands approach a metal ion, they cause the d-orbitals to split in energy.
In an octahedral field, the d-orbitals split into two sets, t two g and e g.
The relative energy difference causes the crystal field splitting energy, denoted by delta.
The spin state depends on the balance between pairing energy and splitting energy.
For a complex like tetraamminecopper(ii) ion, the strong field causes low spin pairing.

faq.q: What is the difference between crystal field theory and crystal field splitting?
faq.a: Crystal field theory is the overall model explaining the splitting. The splitting is the physical result shown in the energy diagram.
asks: What does the splitting actually represent?

faq.q: Why does the geometry matter so much for the splitting pattern?
faq.a: The geometry dictates how the ligands approach the metal ion. This specific arrangement determines which d-orbitals interact most strongly.
asks: Does the shape change the energy levels?
What happens if the shape is tetrahedral?

faq.q: How do I know if a complex will be high spin or low spin?
faq.a: You need to compare the crystal field splitting energy, delta, to the pairing energy. Strong fields mean low spin.
asks: Is there a simple rule for predicting spin state?
Does the metal oxidation state affect this?

faq.q: Does the number of ligands determine the spin state?
faq.a: The nature of the ligands, which determines the field strength, is more important than just the number of ligands present.
asks: Is the ligand identity more important than coordination number?
Can I use the oxidation state to predict spin?

faq.q: Are the t2g and eg orbitals always separated by the same amount?
faq.a: In a perfect octahedral field, the splitting pattern is predictable. However, distortions can cause further deviations from this ideal pattern.
asks: What causes distortions in the field?

facts: The splitting pattern is most pronounced in octahedral complexes.
Strong field ligands cause electrons to pair up in the lower energy set.
Weak field ligands allow electrons to occupy higher energy levels first.
The splitting energy is often denoted by the symbol delta or Δo.

quiz.say: For a metal ion in a weak field ligand environment, how will the d-electrons fill the orbitals?

options.show: Place one electron in each available orbital before pairing.
options.say: Place one electron in each available orbital before pairing.

options.show: Fill all electrons in the lower energy set first.
options.say: Fill all electrons in the lower energy set first.

options.show: Fill the orbitals in order of increasing energy.
options.say: Fill the orbitals in order of increasing energy.

options.show: Fill the orbitals according to the Pauling electronegativity.
options.say: Fill the orbitals according to the Pauling electronegativity.

quiz.why: This follows Hund's rule, maximizing the number of unpaired electrons when the splitting energy is small.

wrong.1: This assumes the pairing energy is very low, which is incorrect for weak fields.
wrong.2: While filling by energy is correct, this option misses the key principle of maximizing spin first.
wrong.3: Electronegativity helps predict field strength, but it is not the direct rule for electron filling.

quiz.say: If the crystal field splitting energy is very large, what is the expected spin state?

options.show: The electrons will fill the higher energy set first.
options.say: The electrons will fill the higher energy set first.

options.show: The spin state will be completely random.
options.say: The spin state will be completely random.

options.show: The splitting energy will be ignored entirely.
options.say: The splitting energy will be ignored entirely.

options.show: The electrons will pair up in the lower energy set (t2g).
options.say: The electrons will pair up in the lower energy set (t2g).

quiz.why: A large splitting energy means pairing up electrons is energetically favorable compared to occupying the higher set.

wrong.0: This ignores the large energy gap, making the higher set prohibitively expensive to occupy.
wrong.1: The filling is governed by predictable energetic rules, not randomness.
wrong.2: The splitting energy is the core concept determining the spin state.

quiz.say: A complex has a small splitting energy. Which filling method is correct?

options.show: Place one electron in each orbital before pairing.
options.say: Place one electron in each orbital before pairing.

options.show: Fill the lower energy set completely before moving up.
options.say: Fill the lower energy set completely before moving up.

options.show: Fill the orbitals in order of increasing energy.
options.say: Fill the orbitals in order of increasing energy.

options.show: The electrons will fill based on the metal's atomic number.
options.say: The electrons will fill based on the metal's atomic number.

quiz.why: When the energy gap is small, it is energetically cheaper to keep the electrons unpaired across the orbitals.

wrong.1: This incorrectly assumes pairing is always favorable regardless of the splitting size.
wrong.2: This general rule is insufficient; Hund's rule takes precedence when the gap is small.
wrong.3: The filling pattern depends on the ligand field, not the atomic number.
